topic: A person learns their childhood best friend doesn't remember them
text: Walking into the damp, dim hallway of memory, I couldn’t help but reflect on the call I just took. Old pal, Jimmy, reaching out after all these years. Always was a smooth talker, but something in his voice was off. Not the usual tremble of desperation or the slick pull of a con. This was different. He mentioned an old friend from his youth who couldn’t place a single memory of him. The silence on the other end of the line stretched, thick as tar. But I’ve been where Jimmy’s headed. Memories fade, Jim. People change. Fact is, if it hurts this much, it means you mattered. Gotta hold onto that, no matter what the other side says. Trust me, I’ve seen the way the past can twist in the cold light of day. Some ties are made to last a lifetime, even if the mind can’t always remember why.
